parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: X-rays for use in medical diagnosis are produced in an X-ray tube. In the X-ray tube, charged particles are accelerated towards a metal target by an applied potential difference (p.d.).
parts.text: State the name of the charged particles that are accelerated by the applied p.d.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how X-rays are produced at the metal target.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the minimum wavelength of X-rays produced when the applied p.d. is $5.80\text{ kV}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
X-rays pass through a medium that has an attenuation coefficient of $1.4\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

Calculate the percentage of the X-ray energy that is absorbed by a $2.8\text{ cm}$ thickness of this medium.
